articles.title: Cobra-d’água no encanamento: como proteger sua casa de invasões | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal não é peçonhento e foi resgatado sem ferimentos em São Vicente (SP). Especialista explicou como animais silvestres conseguem entrar nas residências e listou medidas para evitar esse tipo de situação.
articles.summary: O caso de uma cobra-d’água no encanamento em São Vicente alerta para a invasão de animais silvestres; biólogo recomenda o uso de telas e válvulas de retenção.
articles.body:
O animal foi encontrado na casa de uma moradora na manhã de quarta-feira (4), em São Vicente (SP). — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de São Vicente

Já imaginou estar no banheiro ou na cozinha da sua casa e ser surpreendida por uma cobra-d’água (Erythrolamprus miliaris) saindo por uma tubulação ? Foi exatamente o que aconteceu em uma residência em São Vicente, no litoral de São Paulo.

O caso aconteceu na manhã de quarta-feira (4), em uma residência na Avenida Cellula Matter. Segundo a Prefeitura de São Vicente , equipes da Inspetoria Ambiental foram acionadas depois que a cobra entrou no imóvel pelo encanamento .

A cobra foi capturada em boas condições e devolvida a uma área de mata. Apesar do final feliz, o caso repercutiu em todo o país, gerando dúvidas sobre como um animal pode entrar pela tubulação de uma casa e o que é possível fazer para evitar esse tipo de situação.

🤷‍♀️Como animais silvestres entram em uma casa?

A tubulação exata pela qual a cobra entrou no imóvel não foi informada pela prefeitura. Ao g1 , o biólogo Eric Comin afirmou que animais silvestres, como serpentes, lagartos e até roedores, podem entrar em uma casa por três rotas. São elas:

➡️Subterrâneas: encanamento e rede de esgoto, por meio de ralos sem proteção e vasos sanitários; ➡️Terrestres: frestas embaixo de portas, janelas baixas, tubo de ar-condicionado ou de lavanderia e buracos para fiação; ➡️Aéreas: parte do telhado e forro.

No caso da cobra-d’água, o biólogo explicou que ela entra na tubulação por razões biológicas . "É uma serpente semiaquática, extremamente dependente da água e de áreas úmidas. Para ela, o sistema de tubulação de uma casa não parece uma construção urbana, mas sim uma extensão do seu ambiente natural, como se fosse uma toca inundada ou uma própria margem de um rio", destacou.

Segundo Comin, há ainda a perseguição de alimentos porque a cobra-d'água se alimenta de anfíbios e peixes. "Os sapos e pererecas adoram a umidade e a escuridão de caixas de inspeção, de rede de esgoto e de ralos abertos. Quando ela sai para caçar, segue o cheiro e os rastros de suas presas".

O biólogo destacou que também há a questão de abrigo contra predador e calor . Alguns animais precisam controlar a temperatura do corpo usando o ambiente e os canos oferecem um refúgio escuro, úmido e fresco, além de trazer segurança contra predadores grandes, como aves e mamíferos.

"A cobra-d'água é uma excelente nadadora. Ela nada contra correnteza, consegue ficar submersa por mais de 15 minutos, e as próprias curvas do encanamento acabam não sendo uma barreira", disse o especialista.

"O encanamento funciona como um corredor direto entre a rede de esgoto e o interior da casa. Então, o que precisa fazer? Precisa bloquear esse sistema", acrescentou ele.

Moradora se surpreende ao encontrar cobra dentro de máquina de lavar em Vianópolis, Goiás — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Sílvia das Graças

De acordo com Comin, a estratégia mais eficiente é combinar barreiras físicas com o controle do que atrai esses animais. A pedido do g1 , ele fez uma lista do que é possível fazer para evitar que animais silvestres entrem em uma residência, principalmente pela tubulação e áreas externas. Veja abaixo:

➡️Instalar válvulas de retenção na tubulação, que funcionam como portas, então elas só abrem quando a água for realmente sair, impedindo que qualquer animal suba pelo sentido contrário; ➡️Utilização de telas nos ralos, preferencialmente de aço inoxidável para impedir que roedores, e algumas serpentes, consigam roer essa barreira; ➡️Preferir ralos com vedação automática, que permanece fechado quando não existe fluxo de água; ➡️Manter a tampa do vaso sanitário sempre fechada quando não estiver em uso ➡️Fazer as manutenções dos sifões porque eles acumulam água de propósito para bloquear gases e até bichos; ➡️Combater os roedores e insetos, pois a presença de baratas e ratos é o principal chamariz para cobras e lagartos; ➡️Tratar a gestão de resíduos, ou seja, lixos domésticos e restos de comidas devem estar sempre em sacos bem amarrados; ➡️Nunca deixar ração dos animais de estimação exposta durante a noite ➡️Manter o ambiente ao redor da casa sempre limpo com a grama bem podada e sem pilhas de entulhos; ➡️Tampar frestas de paredes, muros e portas.

A Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) Ambiental de São Vicente orienta a população a não tentar capturar ou manusear animais silvestres encontrados em residências ou áreas urbanas. A corporação pode ser acionada pelo telefone 153.

A Erythrolamprus miliaris é uma serpente conhecida como cobra-d’água, identificada pela variação na coloração, que pode ir do amarelo ao verde — Foto: Charles Boufleur/iNaturalist

A cobra-d’água é uma serpente semiaquática e não peçonhenta, mas pode morder quando se sente ameaçada. A mordida costuma provocar apenas ferimentos leves e dor local. A espécie desempenha um papel importante no equilíbrio ambiental, principalmente no controle de anfíbios e peixes.

O animal é encontrado com frequência em áreas próximas a rios, canais, mangues e outros ambientes úmidos. Locais com vegetação alta, entulho e oferta de alimento, como sapos e rãs, também favorecem sua presença.

Os encontros com a espécie podem ocorrer durante todo o ano, mas são mais frequentes em períodos de chuva.

Mede, geralmente, entre 65 e 90 centímetros de comprimento;

As fêmeas costumam ser maiores que os machos;

É uma espécie ovípara, ou seja, reproduz-se por meio de ovos;

As fêmeas depositam, em média, cerca de dez ovos por período reprodutivo;

A coloração pode variar entre verde-amarelado e preto com tons esverdeados;

Possui manchas pelo corpo que podem formar desenhos semelhantes a um padrão xadrez;

A região ventral, ou barriga, é predominantemente amarela;

articles.title: Painéis de LED viram tendência e transformam comércios e residências | G1
articles.standfirst: LEDFY oferece soluções personalizadas, do projeto estrutural à instalação dos painéis.
articles.summary: LEDFY oferece soluções personalizadas, do projeto estrutural à instalação dos painéis.
articles.body:
Antes presentes principalmente em grandes eventos, shows e publicidade em vias públicas, os painéis de LED agora conquistam fachadas comerciais, projetos arquitetônicos e áreas de lazer residenciais. A tecnologia combina comunicação digital, entretenimento e possibilidades de personalização em diferentes tamanhos e formatos.

Em toda região do triângulo mineiro, a LEDFY atua na comercialização e instalação desses equipamentos, oferecendo projetos sob medida que incluem planejamento estrutural, serralheria, infraestrutura elétrica e montagem. A proposta é reunir as etapas do projeto em um único fornecedor.

Painéis de LED permitem modernizar fachadas e criar novas possibilidades de comunicação visual para estabelecimentos comerciais — Foto: LEDFY/Divulgação

Fachadas comerciais ganham modernidade e novas possibilidades

A fachada é um dos primeiros contatos entre a empresa e o público. Com painéis de LED, estabelecimentos podem exibir logotipos, vídeos, promoções e lançamentos em uma superfície digital, atualizando as informações sem substituir lonas, adesivos ou materiais impressos a cada campanha.

A solução também permite padronizar a comunicação visual de diferentes unidades e integrar o painel à arquitetura do imóvel. Lojas, restaurantes, clínicas, concessionárias, supermercados e outros negócios podem adaptar a tecnologia à sua identidade e às características da fachada.

Tecnologia LED também transforma áreas de lazer residenciais

Em residências, os painéis ampliam as possibilidades de entretenimento em áreas gourmet, varandas e espaços próximos a piscinas. Telas de grandes dimensões podem transformar encontros com familiares e amigos em experiências para assistir a jogos, shows ou filmes.

Além do lazer, os equipamentos podem compor projetos arquitetônicos personalizados. Em áreas externas, é essencial selecionar painéis adequados às condições de luminosidade e exposição ao clima.

Painéis de LED ampliam as possibilidades de entretenimento em áreas gourmet e ambientes de lazer residenciais. — Foto: LEDFY/Divulgação

Diferentes tamanhos e formatos para cada projeto

Formados por módulos, os painéis de LED permitem configurações que vão de telas compactas a grandes superfícies e formatos especiais. Assim, podem acompanhar as proporções de uma fachada comercial ou se adaptar às dimensões de um espaço residencial.

A LEDFY desenvolve cada solução considerando distância de visualização, luminosidade, finalidade de uso, condições estruturais e integração com o ambiente. Na prática, a tecnologia se adapta ao projeto do cliente, e não o contrário.

A estrutura modular dos painéis de LED permite desenvolver soluções personalizadas para diferentes espaços e aplicações — Foto: LEDFY/Divulgação.

Controle na palma da mão: conteúdo atualizado pela internet

Com sistemas de gerenciamento conectados à internet, é possível atualizar imagens, vídeos e campanhas pelo celular ou computador, sem estar fisicamente próximo ao painel. Um lojista, por exemplo, pode trocar uma promoção mesmo fora do estabelecimento.

A tecnologia também pode facilitar a gestão de telas em diferentes unidades e permitir o agendamento de conteúdos por horário ou data, conforme os recursos do sistema utilizado. Em casa, o controle remoto torna mais prática a seleção do que será exibido.

Com gerenciamento remoto pela internet, os painéis de LED podem ter seus conteúdos atualizados diretamente pelo celular, de qualquer lugar, oferecendo praticidade e autonomia aos usuários — Foto: LEDFY/Divulgação.

Da criação do projeto à instalação: tudo em um só lugar

A implantação de um painel de LED exige mais do que escolher a tela: pode envolver dimensionamento, estrutura metálica, adequações elétricas e montagem especializada. Para simplificar o processo, a LEDFY reúne a comercialização dos equipamentos, o projeto estrutural, a serralheria, a infraestrutura elétrica e a instalação.

Com as etapas planejadas de forma integrada, o cliente reduz a necessidade de coordenar fornecedores diferentes. A solução atende tanto à modernização de fachadas e à padronização de redes quanto à criação de ambientes residenciais de entretenimento.

LEDFY reúne projeto estrutural, serralheria, infraestrutura elétrica e instalação para oferecer soluções completas aos clientes. — Foto: LEDFY/Divulgação.

Quer transformar seu espaço com painéis de LED?

Seja para destacar a comunicação visual de uma empresa ou criar uma nova experiência de lazer em casa, a LEDFY desenvolve projetos personalizados para diferentes necessidades. Conheça as possibilidades e solicite um orçamento.

articles.title: Quando cai o 13º salário em 2026? Veja valores e quem tem direito | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeira parcela deve ser paga até 30 de novembro, e a segunda, até 18 de dezembro. Veja como calcular o benefício e quais são os descontos aplicados.
articles.summary: Primeira parcela deve ser paga até 30 de novembro, e a segunda, até 18 de dezembro. Veja como calcular o benefício e quais são os descontos aplicados.
articles.body:
Quando cai o 13º salário em 2026? Veja prazos, valores e quem tem direito — Foto: Marcello Casal Jr.

Novembro mal começou, e os trabalhadores com carteira assinada já estão de olho no pagamento do 13º salário. Considerado um “salário extra”, o benefício é garantido por lei e costuma ser pago em duas parcelas, com prazos definidos.

A primeira parcela deve ser depositada até 30 de novembro, que cai em uma segunda-feira. Já a segunda parcela tem prazo até 20 de dezembro e inclui os descontos obrigatórios.

Neste ano, porém, a segunda parcela do 13º salário deve ser paga até 18 de dezembro, já que o prazo legal de 20 de dezembro cai em um domingo.

O pagamento também terá mudanças na tributação do Imposto de Renda . Trabalhadores que recebem até R$ 5 mil por mês terão isenção do imposto. Já aqueles com rendimentos acima desse valor poderão ter uma redução no desconto, conforme a faixa salarial e as regras aplicáveis.( entenda como funciona )

O valor total pago depende do salário bruto do empregado e do tempo trabalhado ao longo do ano, o que costuma gerar dúvidas entre os trabalhadores.

Pensando nisso, o g1 reuniu as principais dúvidas sobre o tema e responde abaixo:

Qual é o tempo mínimo de registro para ter direito ao 13º?

Como funciona o 13º proporcional para quem foi demitido ou pediu demissão?

Quais são os prazos legais para o pagamento do 13º?

O empregador pode antecipar ou parcelar o 13º de outras formas?

Estagiários, trabalhadores temporários e autônomos têm direito ao 13º?

Todo trabalhador contratado pelo regime da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) tem direito ao 13º salário . Isso inclui empregados domésticos, rurais, urbanos e avulsos.

Além dos trabalhadores da iniciativa privada, aposentados e pensionistas do INSS também recebem o benefício, conforme previsto na legislação brasileira.

O advogado trabalhista Luís Gustavo Nicoli explica que o direito é garantido mesmo para quem não completou um ano na empresa .

"O pagamento é proporcional ao tempo trabalhado. Ou seja, mesmo que o funcionário tenha sido contratado em julho, ele ainda receberá o valor referente aos meses em que esteve na empresa", afirma.

2. Qual é o tempo mínimo de registro para ter direito ao 13º?

Para que um mês seja incluído no cálculo do 13º salário, o trabalhador precisa ter trabalhado pelo menos 15 dias naquele período . Ou seja, não é necessário ter trabalhado o mês inteiro para que ele entre na conta.

" Cada mês com mais de 15 dias de trabalho conta como um mês integral para o cálculo do 13º . Se o empregado trabalhou menos de 15 dias em um determinado mês, aquele período não será considerado no cálculo do benefício”, explica Luís Gustavo.

3. Como é feito o cálculo do 13º salário?

O valor do 13º salário é proporcional ao tempo de serviço no ano. Para calcular, é preciso dividir o salário bruto mensal por 12 (referente aos meses do ano) e multiplicar pelo número de meses trabalhados . O resultado é o valor total do benefício, que normalmente é pago em duas parcelas.

📒 POR EXEMPLO: Se uma pessoa foi contratada em março por um salário bruto de R$ 7 mil , precisará dividir esse valor por 12 . O resultado, de R$ 583,33 , deve então ser multiplicado por nove (quantidade de meses trabalhados). Assim, o valor total a ser recebido por essa pessoa no 13º é de R$ 5.250 .

Na base de cálculo entram o salário-base, adicionais como insalubridade, periculosidade e adicional noturno, além da média de horas extras e comissões .

Já benefícios eventuais ou indenizatórios, como vale-transporte ou auxílio-alimentação, não entram na conta.

A primeira parcela corresponde à metade do valor calculado, enquanto a segunda parcela vem com os descontos obrigatórios, como INSS e Imposto de Renda .

4. Como funciona o 13º proporcional para quem foi demitido ou pediu demissão?

Quem foi demitido sem justa causa tem direito ao 13º proporcional , calculado com base nos meses trabalhados no ano. O mesmo vale para quem pediu demissão voluntariamente: o benefício é pago de forma proporcional ao tempo de serviço.

“O trabalhador que foi dispensado por justa causa perde o direito ao 13º salário ”, explica Nicoli. Por isso, é essencial entender o tipo de desligamento para saber se o benefício será pago ou não.

5. Quais são os prazos legais para o pagamento do 13º?

A primeira parcela do 13º salário deve ser paga até 30 de novembro , que cai em uma segunda-feira. Já a segunda parcela tem prazo até 20 de dezembro, mas, neste ano, a data cai em um domingo. Por isso, o pagamento deve ser antecipado para sexta-feira, 18 de dezembro , para respeitar o prazo legal.

Algumas empresas permitem a antecipação da primeira parcela — que, nesses casos, é paga junto com as férias do empregado —, desde que o pedido tenha sido feito até janeiro do mesmo ano. Essa antecipação é permitida por lei, mas o pagamento deve respeitar os prazos máximos estabelecidos.

6. O empregador pode antecipar ou parcelar o 13º de outras formas?

Sim, o empregador pode antecipar o pagamento do 13º salário, inclusive quitando o valor integral de uma só vez. No entanto, essa antecipação deve respeitar os prazos legais: até 30 de novembro para a primeira parcela e até 20 de dezembro para a segunda.

➡️ O que não é permitido, segundo a legislação trabalhista, é dividir o pagamento em mais de duas parcelas .

“A CLT e o Decreto 57.155/1965 estabelecem que o 13º deve ser pago em até duas vezes. Qualquer outra forma de parcelamento não está prevista na lei”, esclarece Nicoli.

7. Estagiários, trabalhadores temporários e autônomos têm direito ao 13º?

Estagiários não têm direito ao 13º salário , pois o estágio é regido por uma legislação específica (Lei 11.788/2008) e não configura vínculo empregatício.

Autônomos e prestadores de serviço — como os que trabalham como pessoa jurídica, os chamados PJs — também não têm direito ao benefício.

"Como não há relação de emprego, não se aplica a eles o pagamento do benefício", explica o advogado.

Por outro lado, trabalhadores temporários , contratados conforme a Lei 6.019/1974, têm direito ao 13º , pois há vínculo de emprego durante o período do contrato.

O atraso no pagamento do 13º salário pode gerar multa para o empregador. O trabalhador que não receber o benefício dentro do prazo pode denunciar a empresa à Superintendência Regional do Trabalho, órgão responsável por fiscalizar o cumprimento das leis trabalhistas.

Por isso, é importante que as empresas se organizem para fazer os depósitos nas datas corretas.

articles.title: Chefe ruim e falta de crescimento fazem profissional pedir demissão | G1
articles.standfirst: Guia Salarial 2027 da Michael Page mostra que falta de crescimento e liderança desmotivadora estão entre os principais motivos para profissionais deixarem uma empresa.
articles.summary: Guia Salarial 2027 da Michael Page mostra que falta de crescimento e liderança desmotivadora estão entre os principais motivos para profissionais deixarem uma empresa.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa mostra trabalhador diante de um computador. Estresse crônico, assédio e sobrecarga de tarefas estão entre os riscos psicossociais relacionados ao trabalho. — Foto: Reprodução/Adobe Stock.

A relação com o chefe pesa na decisão de procurar outro emprego para 90% dos profissionais brasileiros. Apesar disso, apenas 4% das empresas apontam a liderança como principal estratégia para reter talentos.

Os dados são do Guia Salarial 2027 da Michael Page , que ouviu 5.762 profissionais e 1.955 empresas e analisou mais de 400 cargos em 15 setores da economia. (veja abaixo quais são)

Segundo o levantamento, a falta de perspectiva de crescimento é um dos principais motivos para um trabalhador buscar novas oportunidades, citada por 69% dos entrevistados.

Em seguida aparece a liderança desmotivadora, mencionada por 60% . Já a remuneração, embora seja um dos principais fatores na hora de aceitar uma proposta de emprego, ocupa apenas a terceira posição entre os motivos que levam profissionais a deixar uma empresa.

"Salário importa, mas o estudo mostra que crescimento e liderança têm um peso ainda maior na decisão de ficar ou sair de uma empresa. A empresa que tenta resolver retenção apenas com remuneração pode estar olhando para o problema errado", avalia Ricardo Basaglia, CEO da Michael Page Brasil.

A pesquisa também mostra que a cultura organizacional tem ganhado relevância. Mais da metade dos entrevistados (56%) afirmou que aceitaria ganhar menos para trabalhar em uma empresa alinhada aos seus valores .

Ainda assim, a liderança aparece atrás da cultura corporativa, dos benefícios e da reputação da marca entre as principais estratégias de retenção adotadas pelas companhias.

Outro dado que chama atenção é que 57% dos profissionais não receberam aumento salarial nos últimos 12 meses. Por outro lado, as perspectivas para 2027 são mais positivas: 30% das empresas pretendem conceder reajustes acima do dissídio, ante 20% registrados na edição anterior do estudo.

Quanto ganham os profissionais em cargos de liderança?

Além de mapear os fatores que influenciam a retenção de talentos, o estudo também traz um panorama das remunerações praticadas para cargos de liderança e gestão em diferentes setores da economia.

De acordo com o Guia Salarial 2027, posições de gerência podem pagar entre R$ 14 mil e R$ 90 mil por mês , dependendo do segmento de atuação, do porte da empresa e da complexidade das responsabilidades.

O levantamento analisou mais de 400 cargos distribuídos em 15 setores da economia brasileira:

Os maiores salários identificados pelo levantamento estão concentrados em cargos de alta liderança. No varejo, um general manager pode receber até R$ 140 mil por mês , a maior remuneração mapeada pelo estudo.

Em seguida aparecem os setores de bancos e serviços financeiros e de saúde e ciências da vida, com salários que podem chegar a R$ 100 mil mensais.

Na outra ponta, o menor piso salarial encontrado foi o de coordenador de mídias sociais, na área de marketing, com R$ 6 mil por mês. O estudo também destaca a valorização de profissionais ligados à inteligência artificial: em tecnologia, um especialista em IA tem salário inicial de R$ 12,6 mil mensais.

Maiores salários por setor do Guia Salarial 2027

Menores salários por setor do Guia Salarial 2027

Aumentos salariais e retenção de talentos

O levantamento mostra que 57% dos profissionais não receberam aumento salarial nos últimos 12 meses. Entre os que tiveram reajuste, 54% disseram que o aumento ocorreu por mérito, 27% por dissídio, 13% em razão de uma promoção e 6% após uma contraproposta da empresa para evitar sua saída.

Do lado das companhias, 30% pretendem conceder aumentos acima do reajuste obrigatório em 2027 . Na edição anterior do estudo, esse percentual era de 20% . Apesar da alta, 45% das empresas afirmaram que não pretendem oferecer reajustes além do dissídio, enquanto 24% ainda não definiram sua política salarial.

A dificuldade de atrair profissionais qualificados continua sendo o principal desafio das empresas, apontado por 69% delas. O índice, porém, caiu em relação à edição anterior, quando era de 73%.

Já a rotatividade permanece como um problema: 40% das companhias registram turnover superior a 20% ao ano . No varejo, o percentual chega a 50%.

Outro dado do estudo mostra que 56% dos profissionais aceitariam ganhar menos para trabalhar em uma empresa cuja cultura estivesse alinhada aos seus valores.

Inteligência artificial ainda tem pouco peso nas contratações

A pesquisa também analisou a adoção da inteligência artificial no ambiente corporativo. Segundo o levantamento, 92% das empresas já identificam algum ganho concreto com o uso da tecnologia , como aumento de produtividade, automação de tarefas repetitivas e melhoria na qualidade das entregas.

Apesar disso, apenas 15% consideram o conhecimento em inteligência artificial um requisito importante na contratação de profissionais. Outros 30% afirmam que a habilidade ainda não influencia suas decisões de recrutamento.

Na remuneração, 23% das empresas já utilizam o domínio da tecnologia como critério para definir salários. Outros 37% estão avaliando essa possibilidade, enquanto 32% descartam considerar a competência para esse fim.

Entre os trabalhadores, 57% acreditam que profissionais que dominam inteligência artificial deveriam receber salários maiores.

Os resultados mostram que, embora a remuneração continue sendo um fator importante, crescimento profissional, cultura organizacional e qualidade da liderança têm peso cada vez maior na permanência dos profissionais nas empresas.

articles.body: In 1990, Richard Phillip Eckert and Virginia Eckert Garrett donated a cave in Mason County, Texas, to The Nature Conservancy in honour of their father and grandfather. The gift ensured the bats would be permanently protected. According to the Conservancy, about four million female Mexican free-tailed bats now use the Eckert James River Bat Cave Preserve each year from May to September, and many give birth to a single pup in June. The family set one condition: the land around the cave must stay open to the public for enjoyment and education, as it had been for more than 100 years.Why does a Texas cave shelter four million Mexican free-tailed batsAccording to TNC's preserve page, the cave is "one of the largest bat nurseries in the nation". The page says about four million female bats inhabit the preserve from May through September. Many of the females give birth to a single pup in June. The pups join their mothers in flight at about five weeks of age and stay with them until the colony returns to Mexico in October.The preserve's brochure gives the same figures and names the species as the Mexican free-tailed bat. It describes the site as lying in the Texas Hill Country, southwest of the town of Mason. The brochure says the bats use the cave to give birth and raise their pups before returning to Mexico. It also states that the preserve is home to one of the largest aggregations of warm-blooded animals in the world.How did the Eckert family protect the Texas bat caveTNC's page says the cave's history is closely tied to the Eckert family. W. Phillip Eckert bought the ranch on which the cave stands in 1907. In the early 1900s, he mined the bat guano in the cave and sold it to local farmers as crop fertiliser. His son, Lee Eckert, continued the guano mining and his father's legacy of bat conservation. When Lee died in 1967, he left the site to his wife and children.In 1990, Richard Phillip Eckert and Virginia Eckert Garrett donated the cave to TNC. The preserve page says the gift honoured their father and grandfather, and that it ensured the bats would be permanently protected. The donation came with one condition: the land around the cave must remain open to the public for enjoyment and education, as it had been for more than 100 years. TNC says it is happy to continue that tradition. The brochure gives the same account of the family's history and the donation.How do Mexican free-tailed bats benefit the ecosystemTNC's page explains that, like all bat species, the Mexican free-tailed bats play a part in the region's ecology. Each night they search thousands of acres of countryside for food. Each bat eats close to its body weight in mosquitoes and other insects, including crop pests such as cutworm and corn borer moths. The brochure adds that some bat species act as agents of seed dispersal and cross-pollination.These benefits depend on roosting sites such as the Bat Cave remaining undisturbed. Disturbance usually leads either to a roost being abandoned completely or to the decimation of the bat population. Because free-tailed bats have a low birth rate, TNC states that a single act of vandalism can destroy a colony. The brochure says the population has declined dramatically in some areas of the country, largely because of the disturbance and destruction of roost sites by humans. It adds that the bats give birth to only a single pup each year, so the population recovers slowly.How does TNC protect the Mexican free-tailed bat colonyAccording to TNC, it developed a cooperative management plan with Bat Conservation International. The plan prevents people from entering the cave during maternal activity, controls visitation, monitors the bat population and protects the cave's opening. Scientific research continues at the site, and the cave remains open to scientists for most of the year. The brochure says the preserve is an important research site that helps to inform bat conservation strategies across Texas.Each summer the preserve also serves as an educational site. TNC says visitors can watch the bats flutter and chirp around the cave mouth an hour or two before sunset. The bats first fly in a large, low circle and then spiral upwards into a funnel that reaches several hundred feet into the sky. This lasts about an hour. The brochure describes the preserve as "a true wilderness area" with no electricity, restrooms, water or food, and it does not allow pets. It says the cave is about 500 yards from the parking area along a trail that is not wheelchair accessible. The brochure lists a fee of $5 per adult, with children aged five and under admitted free. TNC's page states that the 2026 viewing season has ended and the preserve is closed until summer 2027.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Pregnancy is not a disease': Bengaluru mom explains why she applied lipstick during labour, says makeup helped her distract herself from contractions
articles.summary: A few contractions, a lipstick in hand and a woman choosing to experience one of the most intense moments of her life on her own terms.
articles.body: A few contractions, a lipstick in hand and a woman choosing to experience one of the most intense moments of her life on her own terms. For Myra Sharma, a Bengaluru and Patna-based engineer and content creator, applying lipstick while in labour was not about looking glamorous or pretending that childbirth was easy. It was simply her way of keeping herself occupied and finding a little comfort during a physically demanding experience.When she shared a video of herself getting ready amid labour contractions on Instagram, it quickly caught people's attention. While some appreciated her choice, the post also brought up a familiar issue faced by women: why are their personal choices so often questioned, especially during pregnancy and motherhood? Myra, however, had an explanation for her decision. And it went beyond makeup.Why Myra chose lipstick over sitting idle during labourIn her Instagram video, Myra was seen applying lipstick while experiencing labour contractions. Anticipating that people might judge her without understanding the situation, she asked viewers to read her caption before forming an opinion. She explained that applying makeup was a way to distract herself from the discomfort. Rather than screaming or simply lying down, she wanted to keep her mind occupied with something she enjoyed.Explaining her decision, she wrote, "Because instead of screaming or just lying down like a patient, I wanted to distract myself and divert my mind." For Myra, it was a personal coping mechanism. She was not suggesting that labour pain was easy or that every woman should handle it the same way. She was simply choosing an activity that helped her feel comfortable during the experience.‘Pregnancy is not a disease’: Her second pregnancy made the experience differentAnother important reason behind Myra's decision was that this was her second pregnancy. Having already experienced childbirth, she said she understood what was happening and knew what worked for her. She also pointed out that labour pain does not necessarily remain constant throughout the process. It comes and goes in waves, giving women moments between contractions. "My pregnancy era ends here, forever. In this phase of life, I wanted to enjoy every bit of it," she wrote.She further explained, "Labour pain doesn't last continuously; it comes and goes in waves." Her words reflected how she wanted to approach this particular chapter of her life. Rather than allowing the difficult moments to define the entire experience, she wanted to enjoy whatever parts of it she could. Myra also shared that she enjoys documenting her life. Looking presentable, even during challenging situations, is something she personally likes. For her, applying lipstick was not an attempt to make childbirth look effortless but a small way of feeling like herself.Past surgeries and a different pain thresholdMyra also addressed why she was comfortable making this choice. She revealed that she had undergone multiple surgeries in the past and believed she had developed a high tolerance for pain. "I have a high pain tolerance, having undergone multiple surgeries in the past," she wrote. However, she was careful not to suggest that her experience should become a standard for other women. She acknowledged that every woman has a different pain threshold and that no two delivery journeys are exactly alike. What feels manageable for one person may be overwhelming for another.Her message was also directed at people who are quick to comment on how a pregnant woman should behave. She reminded viewers that women should be allowed to experience pregnancy and childbirth in ways that feel right to them, without having to meet someone else's expectations.Social media users share their own labour experiencesMyra's post also encouraged other women to share how they kept themselves occupied or comfortable during labour. One social media user related to her choice and wrote, "Putting lipstick on to change my mood is my all-time favourite." Another shared a rather different experience, saying, "Do what makes you happy. I was working from home when I went into active labour." Several others appreciated Myra's confidence and appearance. One person commented, "You look beautiful," while another called her an inspiration and questioned why anyone would judge her personal choice.One particularly interesting comment came from a woman who revealed that she had her nails done during active labour to distract herself. However, she added that the nurse eventually removed her nail polish. The responses showed that women can find comfort in different things, even during one of the most physically demanding experiences of their lives. For Myra, the lipstick was never the main story. It was about having the freedom to decide what made her feel better during labour. As she concluded in her post, "If you can't say anything nice, please remember that not every experience has to look the same. And yes, you are absolutely free to judge me in the comment section."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 86-year-old sailor and his dog rescued 460 miles off California after disappearing during a 5,000-mile Pacific voyage for more than two months
articles.summary: An 86-year-old sailor and his dog have been rescued more than two months after disappearing during a voyage across the Pacific Ocean.
articles.body: An 86-year-old sailor and his dog have been rescued more than two months after disappearing during a voyage across the Pacific Ocean. The pair were aboard the sailboat Willow Wind, travelling from Astoria, Oregon, to Pago Pago in American Samoa, when contact was lost on August 20. The U.S. Coast Guard was alerted that the sailor was overdue on October 24, before an emergency beacon from his vessel triggered a search three days later. A Coast Guard aircraft eventually located the disabled sailboat about 460 miles off San Diego, leading to a rescue involving merchant mariners and Coast Guard crews.86-year-old sailor and his dog disappeared during a Pacific voyageThe sailor had set out from Astoria, Oregon, aboard the Willow Wind with his dog, bound for Pago Pago in American Samoa. The planned journey covered roughly 5,000 miles across the Pacific. According to PEOPLE, nobody had heard from the pair since August 20. Authorities were not immediately aware of their situation, and the sailor was eventually reported overdue on October 24. The Coast Guard then began coordinating a search for the missing vessel and its occupants. The case involved an elderly sailor travelling a long ocean route far from the California coast.Emergency beacon helped rescuers locate the missing sailboatA breakthrough came on October 27, when an emergency transmitter registered to the Willow Wind sent an alert. The Coast Guard responded by deploying aircraft and the cutter Robert Ward, while nearby vessels were also asked to assist. A C-27 Spartan aircraft from Coast Guard Air Station Sacramento eventually located the sailboat about 460 miles off San Diego. The discovery came more than two months after the sailor and his dog had last been heard from. The vessel was still drifting at sea, giving rescuers a precise location from which to organise the recovery operation.Rough seas initially prevented the sailor and dog from being rescuedThe motor vessel Grand Orion reached the Willow Wind early on October 28, but difficult sea conditions initially made it too dangerous for the crew to bring the sailor and his dog aboard. Later that day, conditions allowed the merchant vessel's crew to complete the rescue at about 5:36 p.m. The Willow Wind had damaged sails and was left adrift after the pair were taken to safety. The successful recovery came after a lengthy period without communication and followed a coordinated response involving aircraft, a Coast Guard cutter and commercial vessels.Coast Guard helicopter flew the pair back to CaliforniaAs per Fox News, the rescue operation continued the following morning when a Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted the sailor and his dog from the Grand Orion. The vessel was then about 170 miles west of Ventura, California. The pair were transported to San Diego, where the sailor was taken to Scripps Mercy Hospital for medical evaluation. PEOPLE reported that emergency medical personnel found him weak and having difficulty walking, but he had no major injuries. The Coast Guard did not provide further details about the dog's condition. The rescue therefore ended with both survivors safely removed from the disabled sailboat.Damaged sails left the 86-year-old sailor stranded far offshoreThe condition of the Willow Wind appears to have played a major role in the emergency. By the time rescuers located the vessel, its sails were damaged, and it was drifting in the Pacific. The boat was ultimately left behind after the sailor and his dog were transferred to the Grand Orion. The distance from the California coast also complicated the response, with the vessel initially located about 460 miles from San Diego. The rescue required coordination between Coast Guard aircraft, a cutter and commercial mariners already operating in the region.Coast Guard stresses importance of emergency communication at seaCoast Guard Cmdr. Jason Nguyen said the successful rescue highlighted the value of emergency communication equipment and having a float plan so someone onshore knows a vessel's intended route. In this case, the emergency transmitter aboard the Willow Wind ultimately provided the crucial alert that allowed authorities to locate the missing sailor and his dog. The pair had gone without contact for more than two months before the beacon signal was received. Their rescue demonstrates how emergency location technology and coordinated responses can become critical when sailors encounter trouble far from shore.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Immigration policy too tough': 5 key takeaways from Trump's 60 minutes interview after midterm setback
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that the war with Iran contributed to the Republican Party's losses in the midterm elections, while conceding
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that the war with Iran contributed to the Republican Party's losses in the midterm elections, while conceding that his administration's deportation drive may have been too harsh and expressing willingness to work with Democrats on immigration reform.In an interview with CBS News on Friday, with a full transcript published on Sunday, Trump offered his assessment of the Republicans' setbacks, saying voters were unhappy with the war, rising petrol prices and what he described as growing dislike of Israel.Asked about vice-president JD Vance's assertion that the Iran war was the reason for the party's defeat, Trump said: "I don't disagree with it."He nevertheless defended his decision to confront Tehran, saying he could not allow Iran to acquire nuclear weapons."My answer is an emphatic yes because you can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he said, adding that he believed the decision would be viewed favourably in the long run.ImmigrationTrump said his administration's crackdown on illegal immigration had both helped and hurt Republicans electorally. While he believed he had received strong support for securing the border and deporting criminals, he acknowledged that the removal of people who had established lives and jobs in the US had caused concern.Asked whether the deportation policy had gone too far, Trump replied: "I think it might be too tough, yeah."He suggested that a compromise with Democrats could allow some immigrants who had lived in the country for years and were working in sectors such as hospitality and landscaping to remain in the US legally, while continuing to remove people involved in serious crimes and drug dealing."I think that's something that's actually doable," he said, adding that several Democrats had already approached him about working together on immigration.Trump also said he would be willing to avoid insulting Democratic lawmakers for six months if that helped secure an agreement. "Very easily," he said when asked whether he could do so.IranThe president maintained that the US had prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and said he was not looking to escalate the conflict further.Asked about the remaining nuclear material in Iran, Trump said: "They have nothing. It's buried under thousands of tons of rock."He also insisted that the Strait of Hormuz was open, saying ships were moving through it, while defending the continued presence of US forces in the region. Trump said countries protected by Washington during the conflict would eventually reimburse the US for the costs of the war.He rejected the suggestion that the US had to make concessions to reopen the waterway, maintaining that American military involvement had been decisive in protecting its allies.Russia-Ukraine warTrump said he believed a deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war was close and claimed the conflict would not have begun had he been president at the time.Asked about the biggest obstacle to a settlement, he cited the hostility between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy."I believe that that war is going to end, and it's gonna end soon. And the only reason it's gonna end is because of me," Trump said.He declined to say whom he trusted more between Putin and Zelenskyy, but rejected the suggestion that the Russian president was delaying negotiations. Trump also defended his record on Moscow, saying he had been tougher on Russia than any other US president through trade measures and sanctions.On the terms of a possible settlement, he said Ukraine would emerge with "a little bit different shape".Cabinet changesTrump indicated that changes could be made to his administration following the Republican losses, although he said he remained satisfied with his Cabinet."I love my Cabinet. I think they're good. But I'll do-- be doin' maybe a few changes," he said.He also expressed confidence in defence secretary Pete Hegseth, whose position has faced calls for scrutiny over his handling of the Iran conflict.AI and ChinaTrump described artificial intelligence as a crucial area of competition with China, arguing that the US could not afford to fall behind Beijing."Whoever wins that race wins," he said, adding that the risks associated with AI were not as serious as some industry figures suggested and could be managed.He said he was open to safeguards on the technology but warned against regulations that could leave the US at a disadvantage. "I don't mind guardrails," Trump said, while arguing that China had fewer restrictions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Indonesia wildfires: One dead after firefighting helicopter crash
articles.summary: An Indonesian crew member was killed, while an Australian and New Zealander were rescued after the crash.
articles.body:
One person has died after a helicopter crashed into a river in Indonesia during a mission to fight wildfires in South Kalimantan .

An Indonesian crew member was killed, while two others on board - an Australian and New Zealander - were "found safe" and taken to hospital for treatment, according to Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency.

Investigations into the accident are ongoing, the agency said on Sunday, adding that it could continue its firefighting operations.

For months, parts of Indonesia have been battling wildfires that have shrouded large swathes of South East Asia in toxic haze. The blazes in forests and peatlands are fuelled by a dry season that has been exacerbated by El Niño.

Videos posted by Indonesia's disaster authorities and circulating on social media show the helicopter hovering over the river with a helicopter bucket - a collapsible container typically used to douse water over fires - before it nosedives into the water.

Other videos show rescuers later reaching the partially submerged helicopter by boat.

The deceased crew member was named by Indonesian authorities as Yayan Supyansuri. The two men rescued were Michael John Betterridge, an Australian national, and Hugh Andrew John Page, a New Zealander, according to a statement from disaster authorities.

The fallen chopper, a Super Puma H-225, was owned by a company that disaster authorities had contracted for the firefighting operations, a disaster official told AFP.

The incident comes days after another helicopter crashed in central Kalimantan during a firefighting operation, killing three crew members.

The military said on Saturday that they had managed to retrieve the helicopter's blackbox, which would help their investigations into the cause of the crash.

Despite intensive firefighting efforts, the wildfires in Indonesia this year have been especially difficult to tame due to drought conditions exacerbated by a stronger El Niño.

The raging wildfires sent toxic smog blanketing cities in Indonesia, turning the air amber and triggering a surge in respiratory illnesses in cities across the islands of Kalimantan and Sumatra.

The haze also drifted to neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore, where it has triggered public health concerns.

Foreign governments have sent assistance to help with firefighting efforts, including Australia, which has deployed aircraft and 20 personnel including pilots and paramedics.

articles.title: Trump admits immigration enforcement may have been too 'tough' in first interview since midterms
articles.summary: President Donald Trump conceded his deportation policies may have been too "tough" and suggested that he could make a deal with the incoming Democratic Congress.
articles.body: President Donald Trump admitted that he may have been too "tough" in his immigration enforcement in his first sit-down interview since the midterm elections last week. Trump spoke to CBS News correspondent Ross Douthat about several topics largely related to the Democratic Party's overwhelming wins in last week's midterm elections, which included victories in Republican strongholds like Texas. During their conversation, Douthat asked whether Trump's strict immigration and deportation enforcement likely contributed to Republican losses. CONSERVATIVES STUNNED BY 'CATASTROPHIC' MIDTERM BLUE TSUNAMI, BLAME TRUMP'S IRAN WAR, HIGH GAS PRICES "I think it both helped and hurt," Trump answered. "I think I got an A-plus for closing up the border…I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out." In the extended interview posted online, Trump added, "We had 25 million people come in through Biden over a four-year period, and many of those people were — as you know, they were from prisons, they were drug dealers, they were from mental institutions." However, Trump conceded that many illegal immigrants within the country were "good" people, which likely led to his policies facing backlash. "But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that — that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally. Now, there is a large part of the country that think that they should be put out. And there's a large part of the country that think that they should be allowed to stay if they're good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes. And there's a large group of people who think that they should be allowed to stay." FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM' "So you think your deportation policy — went too far?" Douthat asked. "I think it was — too tough…I think it might be too tough, yeah," Trump responded, adding, "And I think ultimately that hurt me." The president also suggested an immigration deal with the incoming Democratic Congress could be "doable" outside the more extreme groups who either prefer every illegal immigrant to be deported or prefer not to deport any illegal immigrant. articles.title: Moldova launches new power line to Romania to cut reliance on Russia
articles.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu says ‘two more power lines to Romania are on the way’.
articles.body:
Moldova has officially launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid to reduce its reliance on Russian energy.

“For decades, Moscow used energy to blackmail us,” Moldovan President Maia Sandu said on X on Sunday.

“No more: Moldova buys zero Russian gas,” she added.

Moldova, a country of 2.6 million people wedged between Romania and Ukraine, received most of its gas from Russia via its pro-Moscow separatist region of Transnistria and pipelines running through Ukraine.

“Thanks to this project, we are strengthening our electricity transmission capacity, diversifying our means of supply and reinforcing the connection of the Republic of Moldova to the European energy system,” Sandu said during the power line’s inauguration ceremony on Sunday in the capital, Chisinau.

She also said that “two more power lines to Romania are on the way”.

European Commissioner for Energy Marta Kos, who was at the ceremony, said Moldova could now “buy energy where it is cheapest”.

The 400-kilowatt extra-high-voltage line, which runs from the city of Vulcanesti to Chisinau, allows Moldova to cut reliance on the Cuciurgan thermal power plant in Transnistria.

“Every time Moldova dares to choose something other than what Moscow wants, they threaten to cut our electricity,” said Sandu.

Dubbed the “energy independence line”, the power grid was launched two years after the date Moldovan authorities initially promised.

Last month, Moldova’s parliament approved a government-requested state of emergency until November 20 as it tries to ease gas shortages amid soaring world energy prices.

Some in Europe have blamed Moscow for the skyrocketing gas prices, accusing it of withholding additional supplies to put pressure on the continent.

European-aligned states in the Black Sea region say they are experiencing renewed attacks allegedly carried out by Russia.

Last month, Romania blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast, killing one crew member and leaving three others missing.

Ukraine, Romania and Bulgaria have called on NATO to “fast-track the additional surveillance capabilities” to protect commercial shipping in the Black Sea, as fighting in Russia’s war on Ukraine escalates.

NATO said it would send more maritime patrol aircraft , radar systems and drones to the ⁠⁠⁠⁠Black Sea.

articles.title: Trump says he doesn’t disagree with Vance that Iran war fueled GOP losses
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said he doesn’t disagree with JD Vance’s assessment that the Iran war, rising costs and Israel ties contributed to GOP midterm losses.
articles.body: President Donald Trump on Sunday said he does not disagree with Vice President JD Vance's assessment that the Republicans' sweeping midterm losses were caused by the Iran war, rising costs and U.S. relations with Israel. "I don’t disagree with it," Trump said during a CBS 60 Minutes interview. Asked whether he knew Vance was planning to share his take in a post on X, Trump said the vice president was fully transparent with him beforehand "He asked me what do I think," Trump said. VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY' "I said, ‘You write what you want. By the way, what are you going to write?’" Trump added that the one thing he wished Vance would have done differently was share whether the vice president would have made the decision to strike Iran again, given his role in the administration's decision-making process. "The only thing I wish he would've said there, if he felt it," Trump said. "My answer is an emphatic yes, because you can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," Trump said. He said the administration's decision to engage in war with Iran was far more important than the political consequences of losing the midterm elections, arguing that while the decision may be unpopular, the alternative would have been allowing Tehran to obtain a nuclear weapon. "I think, historically, this will be a very good decision. Is it a good decision for today and tomorrow? Maybe not," he said. "I have to go with what's right for our country. If they had a nuclear weapon during my term, I would be excoriated far worse than what's happened." STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE On Wednesday, Vance delivered a blunt assessment of Republicans' midterm losses, which allowed Democrats to regain control of both chambers of Congress in a major blow to the Trump administration. Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts. "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," Vance wrote on X. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night." Like Trump, Vance argued that the political consequences of the war were a "worthwhile cost to pay." "Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost."

articles.title: Two Washington deputies killed trying to rescue possible hostages after woman shot
articles.summary: Two Washington state sheriff's deputies were fatally shot responding to a domestic violence call near Spangle as they tried to rescue potential hostages.
articles.body: Two Washington state sheriff’s deputies were fatally shot as they moved in to rescue possible hostages after a woman called for help following a domestic violence shooting, according to authorities. Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputies Mason Acheson and Parker Perry came under fire from inside the home near Spangle, south of Spokane, as they tried to get in on Nov. 3, the sheriff’s office said. The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office and Spokane Valley Police Department said they were devastated by the shooting and pledged to support the deputies’ families. YOUNG SOUTH DAKOTA DEPUTY DIES THREE DAYS AFTER BEING SHOT DURING A CONFRONTATION AT A HOME "They bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know," the agencies said in a statement. "They are true examples of selfless service and dedication." Deputies first responded around 2:25 p.m. after a woman reported she had been shot. SOUTH CAROLINA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, ANOTHER WOUNDED IN GUNFIGHT WITH SUSPECT WHO HAD EXTENSIVE RECORD The sheriff’s office said they learned the suspect had an active felony warrant and might have access to more weapons. With other victims possibly still inside, they called in SWAT. The woman was taken to the hospital with injuries that appeared to be non-life-threatening. Perry, a K-9 deputy, answered the call with his dog, Brego. He joined the team approaching the house around 3:15 p.m. and forced his way in, the sheriff’s office said. AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND When gunfire struck Perry and Acheson, their teammates fired back, pulled them to cover and began treating their wounds. Authorities called for medical helicopters and closed stretches of Interstate 90 and U.S. Highway 195 to help get the deputies to the hospital, the Washington State Patrol said. Acheson died after being taken to the hospital. Perry remained on life support while arrangements were made for him to donate his organs. The sheriff’s office said he would "continue to serve others with the gift of life." Both men left behind wives and two children. Perry and his wife were expecting their third. WATCH: EVICTION STANDOFF TURNS TO WAR ZONE AS GUNMAN KILLS DEPUTY IN AMBUSH, GETS RUN OVER BY ARMORED VEHICLE Back at the house, Spokane police took over the scene after SWAT teams from Spokane and Kootenai County were called in. A drone sent inside found the suspect dead, the State Patrol said. The Spokane County medical examiner determined that Ryan Larsen, 37, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, The Spokesman-Review reported. The medical examiner also identified two other people killed as Suzanne Larsen, 72, and Rebecca Larsen, 45. A family obituary identified them as Larsen’s mother and sister, according to the newspaper. "It was a very tragic day in Spokane County," Sheriff John Nowels told reporters, according to the outlet. "A lot of families have been affected." Acheson and Perry served in the same Washington Army National Guard infantry battalion, the sheriff's office shared. Acheson enlisted in 2011, rose to sergeant and served in Poland from 2021 to 2022, earning three Army Commendation Medals during his military service. He spent eight years as a Washington State Patrol trooper and firearms instructor before joining the sheriff’s office in 2022. As a SWAT sniper, he watched over teammates as they went into dangerous scenes. AS AN ARMY WIDOW, I WILL NEVER FORGET HOW ORDINARY AMERICANS HONORED MY HUSBAND "In the face of danger, he stepped forward to preserve life," the sheriff’s office said of Acheson. Perry joined the sheriff’s office in 2020 and spent three years on its SWAT team before becoming a K-9 deputy in 2025. He joined the Guard in 2017, rose to captain as a military intelligence officer and earned two Army Commendation Medals. When the call came in near Spangle, he responded "on his own, without prompting," the sheriff’s office said. PHILLY OFFICER MURDERED IN LINE OF DUTY PROMOTED TO SERGEANT AS POLICE FROM AROUND US ATTEND HIS FUNERAL FBI Director Kash Patel honored each deputy in a separate post on X, listing Nov. 4 as Acheson’s end of watch and Nov. 7 as Perry’s. Patel noted that both men were military veterans and pledged the bureau’s support to their families, friends and colleagues. "They will have our full support," he wrote in both posts. The FBI also issued separate tributes to Acheson and Perry. Rep. Michael Baumgartner, R-Wash., said he knew Acheson and his wife from a CrossFit gym and that she was his children’s first piano teacher. "Just wonderful people," he wrote in one tribute. In another post, Baumgartner asked people to keep both families in their prayers and said the deputies "both died protecting our community." Washington Gov. The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office said the Sheriff Community Oriented Policing Effort is accepting donations to help cover the deputies’ funeral expenses, with any remaining funds going to their families. articles.title: Mexico arrests alleged major leader of Jalisco cartel
articles.summary: Rafael Alvarez, alias ‘R2’, was captured with intelligence shared by the ⁠US Drug Enforcement Administration.
articles.body:
Authorities in Mexico have announced the arrest of an alleged leader in the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), one of the country’s two main criminal groups.

Rafael Alvarez, alias “R2”, who is suspected of heading CJNG’s “Los Rs” cell, was arrested in an operation in the city of Zapopan, in the Guadalajara metropolitan area, on Sunday, as a result of intelligence shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)⁠, according to Mexico’s Navy.

“This cell is mainly ⁠linked to extortion, drug trafficking, homicide, illegal deprivation of liberty, kidnapping and attacks against authorities,” Mexico’s Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said.

He added that victims of the group’s extortion included “business owners and avocado producers”.

Harfuch said on X that Alvarez was wounded in a shootout that broke out during the arrest and is receiving medical care.

Alvarez has an outstanding arrest warrant in Mexico for aggravated homicide and another warrant for ⁠extradition to the US, Harfuch also said.

Authorities, including those from Mexico’s National Intelligence Center, also took part in the operation, which captured 19 other people.

Alvarez is linked to the killing of at least 19 people, including last year’s murder of Carlos Manzo, the popular crime-fighting mayor of Uruapan in Mexico’s avocado-producing Michoacan state.

The CJNG, which operates in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan, was designated a “foreign terrorist organisation” by the US government in 2025 and is known for violent tactics and attacks on authorities.

It competes with the Sinaloa Cartel for drug trafficking into the US.

Since the death of the CJNG founder, Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, in a military operation in February, several of its top leaders have been apprehended.

But there are still reports of kidnapping for ransom in the areas where the cartels are active.

An estimated 134,000 people are believed to be missing across Mexico , with Jalisco recording the country’s highest numbers of disappearances.

articles.title: Crackers versus vehicles: What really contributes to Delhi's Diwali pollution?
articles.summary: Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles.
articles.body: Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles. But the latest pollution data suggests the problem is more complex. Pollution can spike sharply in the case of fireworks, but vehicles are one of the biggest contributors to the city’s everyday PM2.5 burden.The real worry is what will happen when these emissions combine with an atmosphere that is already polluted and with bad weather.Vehicles: An endless sourceThe Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) has set up a new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL), which gives a useful picture of Delhi’s pollution mix.Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5 %), road dust (10.9 %) and waste burning (5 %).Even around Diwali the transport contribution was still substantial. Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8, the largest identified source, estimated the IITM’s Decision Support System (DSS). The figure explains why vehicular pollution cannot be seen as a seasonal problem: unlike fireworks, traffic emissions persist throughout the year.What crackers bring to the tableBut firecrackers cause pollution of a different kind of episode. They tend to emit their emissions over a relatively short period of time, and they emit fine particles and gasses that can quickly degrade air quality.The effect was visible on the night of Diwali. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s data reported on November 9 showed that at Akshardham the PM2.5 concentration was at 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11pm. This was an hourly reading, not a 24 hour average, but gives an idea of how intense the spike of pollution was.Delhi’s AQI had already fallen to 382 on November 6, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to CPCB data. It averaged 376 on Diwali November 8, from 369 a day earlier. AQI stood at 368 at 7am on November 9. Of the 54 monitoring stations that reported valid readings, 50 were above 300 and 15 entered the severe category.Weather is the differenceAt the time when fireworks are set off, the Delhi atmosphere is becoming less conducive to dispersing pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System said dispersion is difficult when ventilation index is less than 6,000 square meters per second and average wind speeds are below 10kmph. Low temperatures and temperature inversion can also trap pollutants near the ground.That means fireworks smoke doesn’t just disappear when the party’s over. It adds to the existing emissions from vehicles, industry, dust and regional sources, thus adding to the particulate load.Can't ignore either oneThe latest figures do not allow for simply blaming either crackers or vehicles. Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily. Cracker restrictions can curb the festive spike, but sustained improvement will depend on curbing transport emissions, controlling road dust and industrial pollution, and improving regional coordination. articles.title: US and Iran are quietly negotiating as Middle East remains on edge. Here’s what to know
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said Sunday that renewed US military attacks on Iran are “highly unlikely” if Tehran makes progress toward an agreement on its nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz, offering his clearest indication yet that intensified diplomacy could avert another major round of fighting.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has offered his clearest indication yet that intensified diplomacy could avert another major round of fighting with Iran, in the wake of his party’s disastrous midterm election results. Trump told CNN on Sunday that renewed US military attacks are “highly unlikely” if Tehran makes progress toward an agreement on its nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. He also told CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he was “not looking to” escalate the war. Iran and the United States have quietly been negotiating a sensitive agreement that could avert a return to all-out war and open the door to broader talks. But hopes of a deal are being tempered by Washington, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying Sunday that he “wouldn’t say we’re on the verge of a breakthrough.” Trump has also made clear the military option remains on the table. Both sides and Qatar, which is mediating, have revealed little about the discussions even as diplomatic activity has accelerated since Tuesday’s midterms. What’s changed since the midterms? The Republican losses in the elections have added another dimension to the negotiations, with Vice President JD Vance saying aftewards that the war was among the reasons Republicans lost. Trump told “60 Minutes” that he did not disagree with Vance’s assessment, acknowledging that voters “didn’t like the war.” But he strongly defended the decision to attack Iran, saying that if he had to make the decision again, his answer would be “an emphatic yes.” Iran, meanwhile, has sought to use the election results to press its negotiating position. “American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday. Trump continues to project confidence about the US military position, while Iran has repeatedly threatened to expand the war geographically if it is attacked again. What is being discussed? Both sides have several key demands that are on paper non-starters to the other. Trump seeks to eliminate Iran’s nuclear program, which Tehran sees as a matter of national sovereignty. Publicly, Iran is posturing, insisting it will not negotiate with Washington over the program or reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz unless seven preconditions are met —including ending the war on “all fronts” and lifting a maritime blockade. The specifics are yet to be made public. Hundreds of kilograms of enriched uranium – the material needed to produce a nuclear weapon – remain hidden somewhere in Iran. Tehran has used this stockpile as leverage in its talks with the US. Reports indicate Washington wants the uranium diluted or transferred to another country for safekeeping. It is unclear how far the two sides have progressed on that point. Iran has contended that its nuclear program is for generating energy and not military purposes. For Iran, aside from not ceding ground on its nuclear program or Hormuz, there are key economic goals. As one of the world’s largest oil producers, Iran has found it increasingly difficult to sell crude on global markets under US sanctions. Billions of dollars in Iranian assets held in foreign banks also remain frozen. Washington appears to be weighing relief on these restrictions, a move that could help Tehran ease the severe economic strain on its population amid record inflation. Iran also wants compensation from the US for the killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and his top military commanders by the US and Israel at the start of the war in February. Qatar is mediating between the two sides and circulating a framework document that both Washington and Tehran are amending. The process has been underway for weeks, possibly months, but has intensified in recent days amid fears of fresh strikes. Trump is expected to meet Qatari Prime Minster Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al Thani in Washington on Monday. What’s stopping a deal? So far neither side has been willing to budge on its demands. Before leaving Sunday for the Group of Seven foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested the two sides remained far from an agreement. “Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic.” After successive rounds of open conflict, Tehran’s trust in Washington has almost vanished. Iran has not forgotten that the conflict began while nuclear talks with the US were underway. Iran is concerned that relinquishing any leverage could invite the US and Israel to strike again, leaving it exposed and without effective negotiating tools. If Iran is attacked after opening the Strait of Hormuz and relinquishing control over the enriched uranium, it would be left even more exposed and in a weaker negotiating position. Trump is balancing his ties with Arab partners and Israel – both of which view the Islamic Republic as a threat – and faces scrutiny if he walks away from the war without a major concession from Iran. Tehran also wants to protect its regional proxies and allies in Lebanon, Iraq and Yemen. Those militias have fought on behalf of the Islamic Republic regionally and are loyal to Tehran, but have come under existential pressure over the past three years. In September, Iran’s ally in Yemen, the Houthi rebels, launched a lighting offensive capturing another key maritime chokepoint on the Red Sea – Bab Al Mandeb – and giving Tehran potential influence over another waterway. The Houthis have since ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia in response to Riyadh giving the Yemeni government military support. The US wants Iran not to have capabilities to build a nuclear weapon, including advanced equipment that could allow it to do so. Iran’s Arab neighbors are divided over any agreement that would hand Tehran too much power and cement its desired hegemony. Iran wants to administer the Strait of Hormuz, the maritime corridor through which wealthy Arab states export most of their oil and gas. Control of the waterway would give Tehran decisive influence over what enters and leaves the region. This too would go against the demands of the US, which wants to see open waterways and would be loath to cement one of Iran’s key gains from the war. So, will war resume? There have been some attacks but both sides have played them down, a sign perhaps that neither wants to derail talks. Some outlets report that talks between the two sides have moved closer to agreement. The New York Times has indicated that Iran is willing to re-engage in nuclear negotiations. There has been no independent confirmation but any concessions from Iran on its nuclear program, or even willingness to discuss the topic, would be considered a breakthrough. Yet, despite reports of progress, the risk of an all-out war remains real. The US still has a vast military presence in the Middle East that could launch a major assault on Trump’s orders. Vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz with oil and gas continue to come under Iranian attack. The US is offering a reward of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program and has launched a task force aimed at blocking Tehran from using land routes to move advanced weapons and other materials – signs that Washington is intensifying pressure rather than easing it. Meanwhile, Iranian hardliners who believe Tehran has already emerged victorious in its war with the US are seizing on Trump’s midterm losses to demand that he pay a steeper price for an exit from the conflict. Should a deal be reached by the more reformist-minded Iranian leaders involved in talks they could face opposition at home. Over the past weeks, Iranian military commanders have stepped up their warnings claiming Iran possesses weaponry capable of striking more targets and inflicting even greater damage than before. So, even if Trump is willing to reach deal, it is far from clear if Iran is ready to accept.

articles.title: Pope Leo gives veiled rebuke Argentine leader Milei's austerity measures
articles.summary: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has said Argentina's economy must benefit everyone including the poor, in a diplomatic but pointed critique of President Javier Milei's austerity measures.

The Pope was speaking as he arrived in Buenos Aires, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, only three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

In response, right-wing leader Milei said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today".

This leg of the Pope's journey was expected be the most politically sensitive, with the president's agenda of slashing public spending having been denounced by the Catholic Church for hitting the poorest hardest.

"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," Pope Leo said.

He stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs", and urged that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.

In what appeared to be a rebuke of Milei's combative style and language, the Pope said strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words".

Milei had been particularly outspoken about Leo's predecessor Pope Francis, whom he called "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor.

On Sunday, however, Milei struck a conciliatory tone, calling Francis an "exceptional figure" and "undoubtedly the most important Argentine in history".

He was also keen to welcome the current Pope earlier, writing in a post on X that Argentina awaits "with immense joy".

Pope Leo urged Argentina to safeguard its democracy. "Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community," he said.

In his own address welcoming Leo to Argentina, Milei defended his libertarian policies, saying the rights to life, liberty and property are the backbone of Argentina's constitution and of Western democracies.

The Argentine leader, who has said he will seek re-election next year, is a strong supporter of US President Donald Trump, who has criticised Pope Leo for his opposition to the Iran war .

Pope Leo's trip to Argentina has been described as a homage to Francis, who did not return to his homeland during his own papacy.

The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition".

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

articles.title: Bears survive Buccaneers in chaotic primetime finish after Caleb Williams throws four interceptions
articles.summary: Caleb Williams threw four interceptions but rallied the Bears with a clutch drive capped by a 38-yard strike to Colston Loveland late in the fourth.
articles.body: It was a win for the Bears, but turning the ball over five times is a brutal pill to swallow. In an MVP-or-bust season for Caleb Williams, Sunday night delivered pure whiplash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers — called by emergency replacement Noah Eagle after Mike Tirico was sidelined by an undisclosed health issue. Conventional wisdom says coughing up five turnovers gets you beat every single time, but Chicago found a way to grind out a 27-24 victory. Williams' first career four-interception game nearly doomed Chicago. But even in a messy performance, Caleb proved he can survive three quarters of disastrous football and still win. NBC'S MIKE TIRICO SIDELINED BY HEALTH ISSUE AHEAD OF BEARS VS. BUCCANEERS ON SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL After the Bears built an early 14-0 lead, the offense stalled, opening the door for Tampa Bay to pull even. Just when a flat-footed Chicago squad looked completely stalled out late in the third quarter, cornerback Jaylon Johnson made Baker Mayfield pay for his recklessness, baiting the quarterback into a crushing 67-yard pick-six that kept momentum swinging like a pendulum. BUCCANEERS COLLECT TWO FREAKISH FIRST-HALF SCORES TO DOMINATE PANTHERS – AND, OH, BAKER MAYFIELD IS BACK Yet when everything threatened to collapse after a late Tampa Bay surge, Williams rallied. With 2:51 left and the game knotted at 24, he put together an eight-play, 49-yard drive — highlighted by a 38-yard strike to Colston Loveland — to set up Cairo Santos for the walk-off 38-yard field goal. BEARS PROVE THEY ARE NFC NORTH'S MOST COMPLETE TEAM WITH COMMANDING WIN OVER SEAHAWKS Afterward, Williams was entirely unmoved by the turnover-heavy night. "I'm going to throw until I can't throw anymore," Williams said on the postgame podium. He wrapped up his night with 279 yards, two touchdown passes and four picks. For Tampa Bay, Mayfield choked away the defense's impressive outing. Sacked four times with zero touchdowns, his 243-yard meltdown proved Tampa Bay's QB1 experiment is running on fumes.
